messages:
jas: hi team — day two for me, quick checklist Q: where do you drop a bug vs ask a quick question in slack? also what's the preferred way to signal 'i'm blocked' so someone can help fast?

neha: welcome jas! :wave: Short answer: bugs that need tracking -> file in JIRA (link pinned in #docs) and post a one-line summary in the squad channel with the ticket link. Quick clarifying Qs -> reply in the relevant channel or DM if it's a 1:1. To flag blockers, post in-channel and add :rotating_light: or ping the on-call alias (e.g., @infra-help) for infra blockers.

mike: addendum on signals: use reactions for quick ack (:eyes: or :thumbsup:) so threads don't blow up. If you need synchronous help, say "blocking - 15m help?" and someone usually jumps in. For real production outages, follow the incident playbook in #incidents and ping @eng-oncall-bot.

elaine: about cross-posting: avoid posting the same question in multiple channels. Post once in the most relevant place and mention other channels/users like "cc @data-team". If it's cross-team and you want broad visibility, use #cross-team with a short summary and links. We prefer links to context rather than pasting large logs.

jas: thanks! what about long threads that get noisy — when to move to a doc or ticket?

neha: good call. If the convo needs more than a few back-and-forths or decisions, create a short Google doc or issue and drop the link in the thread with a TL;DR. Use bullet points and action items. That helps onboarding folks follow decisions later.

mike: bot cleanup tip: to stop build notifications, open the message from the CI bot > More actions > Mute or change notification settings. If it's an app you installed, go to Preferences > Notifications > Manage apps. If you're getting DMs from onboarding-bot too often, message it "pause weekly".

onboarding-bot: Hello Jas! You can run `/onboard status` to see remaining checklist items. Reply "pause" to change cadence.

jas: perfect — last tiny etiquette question: thread vs DM for intros?

elaine: post a 1-2 line intro in #new-hires with team and timezone. For longer bios or folks-runway posts, use #random or #people-ops posts. Always add your pronouns if you want.

neha: +1 — and if you want a welcome coffee chat, drop "coffee?" and a time in the thread and someone will claim it. :coffee: 

jas: awesome, appreciate the map and tips :raised_hands:
